text: dsh-hardware-buddy 是一个 DSH 主机插件，通过 USB CDC 将 agent 运行状态、会话数量、近期事件摘要和 token 用量整理成周期心跳并发送到 CodeBuddy StickS3。它还把匹配配置的工具调用接入 DSH 审批流程，在设备在线时显示待审批工具和参数摘要，并将设备按键结果传回审批流程。适合希望把 DSH 状态放到桌面硬件设备上查看、并用实体按键处理工具审批的用户。需要 Node.js 主机、USB 连接的 StickS3 和兼容固件；代码未配置 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-hardware-buddy mirrors DSH session and agent summaries to a StickS3 over USB CDC. Configured tool calls can request approval on the device and relay its button decision to DSH. It requires a Node.js host, USB-connected device, and compatible firmware; it uses no API key or external service.
想把 DSH 的运行状态显示在桌面上的 StickS3 设备上。
能不能用实体按键批准电脑上发起的工具调用？
Show my DSH session activity on a USB-connected desk device.
dsh-hardware-buddy 的功能「设备状态镜像」：汇总 agent 状态、会话变化和近期事件，并按配置的周期发送完整心跳；心跳包含会话与 token 统计等状态数据。
dsh-hardware-buddy 的功能「实体按键审批」：匹配配置的工具会进入审批流程；设备在线时将待审批工具和参数摘要发送到 StickS3，并把设备返回的允许或拒绝决定交回 DSH。

@dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · dsh-hardware-buddy：A self-contained [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) **host (Node.js)** plugin that mirrors agent state onto a CodeBuddy / StickS3 hardware pet over USB CDC, and routes the device's physical **A/B approval buttons** back into the dsh `approval/request` waterfall.

@dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · dsh-hardware-buddy：- 📟 **State mirror** — `agent/status`, `session/*`, `session/event` are aggregated into a compact JSON heartbeat (hard **900-byte** cap) pushed to the device every 3s (not per-event).
- ✅ **Physical approval** — dangerous tools prompt on the device; **A** = allow-once, **B** = reject. Excluded tools (e.g. `MCP__danger_*`) fall through to the dsh Web UI instead.
- 🎙️ **Voice feedback** — device speaks the cheerleader clips (approve / deny / error / idle / boot) when approvals resolve.
- 🔌 **Plug & play** — auto-discovers the StickS3 by USB VID `0x303A` (optionally PID), with a `cu.usbmodem*` / `ttyACM*` name fallback. Tolerates unplug/replug (5s reconnect poll) and never crashes the plugin when the device is absent.

@dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · dsh-hardware-buddy：> This plugin only runs on the **host (Node.js)** side. It deliberately does **not** declare `dsh.client` and must not be bundled into the browser client (it depends on the native `serialport` module).

@dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · Usage：1. Plug the StickS3 into USB. On first boot after a cold start, **pick the device up once** (see "Screen stays frozen" below) so the display activates.
2. Run dsh (web or headless). The plugin auto-connects and the pet shows the agent state.
3. When a dangerous tool needs approval: the device **beeps**, shows the tool + args on the approval screen, and waits.
   - **A** = allow once · **B** = reject · 30s no response = auto-reject (safe default).
4. Approval results are relayed back into dsh's `approval/request` waterfall; the model continues or stops accordingly.

@dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · Screen stays frozen after boot? (not a bug)：After a cold boot, if the device has never been picked up, the firmware waits for an unambiguous orientation before it starts rendering (an upstream CodeBuddy anti-speculation design): a device lying flat gives ambiguous IMU readings, so the screen keeps the boot frame while beeps and buttons keep working. **Pick the device up once** (hold it upright or sideways) — the orientation is then remembered for the rest of the boot, and the screen renders normally even when you put it back down flat.

text: @dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · Safety model (important)：The plugin follows the Cordis **waterfall** rule strictly: *not calling `next()` vetoes the entire chain, including the Web UI*. Therefore the plugin **only takes over** an approval when **(a)** the tool is not on the `excludedTools` list **and (b)** the device is currently online. In every other case — device offline, excluded tool, a missing `agent`/`callId` on the exec, or any internal error — it calls `next()`, delegating to the Web UI / default policy.

@dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · Safety model (important)：The plugin **never** produces an `unavailable` outcome and **never** denies a tool for its own reasons. A timeout or a runtime abort resolves to `cancelled` (which dsh maps to a deny with a "cancelled" reason) — that is dsh's policy, not the plugin refusing.

@dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `No StickS3 CDC port found` | Replug USB; on Linux run `sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER` and re-login; check `pio device list` |
| Device never wakes / no heartbeat | Confirm the DSH firmware (not the stock CodeBuddy BLE build) is flashed |
| Want to see what the plugin is doing | Start dsh with `HB_DEBUG=1` — prints serial discovery, heartbeats, approvals on stderr |
| Approval screen disappears in 3s | Update the plugin (old builds cleared the prompt on the next heartbeat) |

@dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm test      # vitest unit tests (protocol / bridge / approval)
npm run lint  # oxlint
npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit   # type check

The package is fully self-contained: `tsconfig.json` does not extend any external config and `npm install` works without a workspace/pnpm setup. Unit tests do not require a real dsh runtime or a connected device.

@dsh-hardware-buddy/dsh-hardware-buddy README · Probe plugin：`probe.ts` is a standalone companion entry (run inside a real dsh profile) that dumps the live event payloads, the real tool-name list (so `dangerousTools` defaults can be finalized), and the measured VID/PID. It is excluded from the build and from `oxlint src/`.
